candidates.attacker_control: The string field annotated with @Cron(type=...) (typically bound to an HTTP request/body/query parameter). Any input containing characters that are invalid for the selected cron format reaches the template; e.g. a value containing ${...} survives removal of valid cron characters and is echoed back inside the exception message.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that cron-utils contains no eval/exec/reflection/file/URL sinks (searched Runtime, ProcessBuilder, Class.forName, readObject, Properties, new File — none relevant), so this template API is the only data-to-code-class sink. Checked that all String.format/MessageFormat call sites in the descriptor code use literal or resource-bundle patterns (not attacker data). Confirmed the parser really embeds raw input in exception messages (CronParser.java:131, FieldParser.java:263) rather than sanitizing it. Noted that exploitability depends on the host's Bean Validation message interpolator (EL present and enabled), which is outside this repository, and that @Cron is an optional integration rather than the core parser path — these limit severity/confidence and prevent a confirmed-vulnerability claim.
candidates.impact: Message-template / expression-language injection in the validation layer: attacker-controlled `${...}` expressions can be evaluated during message interpolation (potential data exposure such as reading configuration/system properties, and in permissive EL setups code execution), and unresolvable `{...}` templates can break message interpolation (validation failure/error). In cron-utils itself this is unauthenticated input-processing code, so any application exposing an @Cron-validated field inherits the exposure. Impact is bounded by the host provider's interpolator configuration, so no runtime confirmation is claimed.
candidates.prerequisites: Application uses cron-utils' optional javax.validation integration (@Cron on a user-controllable field) with a Bean Validation provider whose message interpolator evaluates templates: Hibernate Validator's default ResourceBundleMessageInterpolator with a javax.el ExpressionFactory/EL implementation on the classpath (typical in Java EE/Dropwizard/Spring Boot with tomcat-embed-el). The violation messages must be surfaced/generated by the application (they are interpolated by the provider regardless of whether they are returned to the client).
candidates.root_cause: CronValidator.isValid catches IllegalArgumentException from cron parsing and passes e.getMessage() straight to context.buildConstraintViolationWithTemplate(e.getMessage()). That message is not sanitized: CronParser.parse wraps failures with String.format("Failed to parse '%s'. %s", expression, e.getMessage()), and FieldParser/ValidationFieldExpressionVisitor build messages that embed the raw field text, so arbitrary attacker characters (including ${...} and {...}) are carried into the string that the Bean Validation provider treats as an interpolatable template. The @Cron annotation's message() default "UNUSED" (Cron.java:16) shows the intent is to emit the exception text as the violation message, which is exactly the untrusted-template pattern.
candidates.title: Untrusted cron expression used as Bean Validation message template in CronValidator
candidates.trace: user string -> @Cron field -> CronValidator.isValid(value) (CronValidator.java:21-29) -> CronParser.parse(value) throws IllegalArgumentException -> message built as "Failed to parse '%s'. %s" with the original expression (CronParser.java:131), including field-level message from FieldParser.stringToInt -> "Invalid chars in expression! Expression: %s Invalid chars: %s" (FieldParser.java:263 / ValidationFieldExpressionVisitor.java:46) -> catch block passes that message to context.buildConstraintViolationWithTemplate(e.getMessage()) (CronValidator.java:33) -> Bean Validation message interpolator treats the string as a template and expands ${...}/{...} constructs.
candidates.unverified: Not executed or runtime-tested (no code execution in this review). Whether the deployed Bean Validation provider evaluates EL for these violation templates (Hibernate Validator version, EL implementation on classpath, use of ParameterMessageInterpolator) was not verifiable from this snapshot. Whether upstream/benchmark ground truth is this issue rather than a parser robustness issue is also unconfirmed.
candidates.weakness_type: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Template Engine (CWE-1336) / Expression Language Injection (CWE-917)

coverage_summary: Read and reviewed all Java main sources in the snapshot (parser incl. CronParser/FieldParser/CronParserField, model/Cron/CompositeCron/SingleCron, CronDefinition/Builders/constraints, field expressions and visitors, mapper (CronMapper/WeekDay/ConstantsMapper), descriptors incl. DescriptionStrategy/TimeDescriptionStrategy/DescriptionStrategyFactory/NominalDescriptionStrategy and the descriptor.refactor package, execution-time engine SingleExecutionTime/ExecutionTimeBuilder/CompositeExecutionTime and all value generators, StringValidations/StringUtils/Preconditions/DateUtils/WeekendPolicy, converters, CronBuilder and validation (@Cron/CronValidator)) plus pom.xml, README, resource bundles and CI/quality config. The single submitted candidate is in com.cronutils.validation; the rest are documented as rejected leads or checked-and-clean areas (no files/exec/deserialization/JNDI/reflection sinks, no externally controlled String.format/MessageFormat patterns).
limitations: No test sources are included in the snapshot, so intended behavior/regression tests could not be consulted.

No compilation, execution, fuzzing, or runtime verification was performed (read-only review); the EL evaluation behavior of the host Bean Validation provider is assumed from the standard Hibernate Validator default message interpolator, not observed.

The snapshot is a single version (pom.xml 9.1.5); no fix/patched version or git history is available to diff against, so it cannot be confirmed which upstream issue/ground truth this snapshot corresponds to.
I could not use external advisory data (no web access); the candidate is based solely on source-level data flow and the semantics of the Bean Validation API named in the code.

Attacker-controlled inputs other than the cron string itself (e.g. serialized CronDefinition/FieldConstraints, custom ResourceBundle strings, custom mondayDoWValue definitions) were considered only briefly; their exploitability depends on the embedding application and remains uninspected.

rejected_leads.lead: CronParser composite '|' parsing indexes s.split("\\|")[j] with j up to the max alternative count across fields (CronParser.java:97-107); mismatched alternatives (e.g. 5-field input with one field having 2 and another 4 alternatives) throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, which is not caught by CronValidator (only IllegalArgumentException is).
rejected_leads.reason: Reachable only as an uncaught runtime exception (availability/robustness bug). Impact is a single failing parse/HTTP 500 rather than memory corruption, injection, or resource exhaustion; weaker than the template-injection candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: FieldParser.parseOnWithHash does array[1] after exp.split("#") without checking length (FieldParser.java:170-184), so input like '1#' throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of IllegalArgumentException.
rejected_leads.reason: Same class of input-validation crash; low impact and no privilege boundary crossed.

rejected_leads.lead: DateUtils.findIdx uses pivot = (endidx-startidx)/2 rather than startidx+(endidx-startidx)/2, which can oscillate between (1,3) and (2,3) for 4+ holidays and recurse until StackOverflowError (DateUtils.java:41-64).
rejected_leads.reason: Holiday list and dates are application-supplied (not attacker-controlled in the reviewed flow) and workdaysCount has no in-repo callers, so attacker control and reachability are unproven.

rejected_leads.lead: SecondsDescriptor.describe(FieldExpression, boolean) recurses into itself for Always and Between instances (SecondsDescriptor.java:44-62) causing StackOverflowError.
rejected_leads.reason: SecondsDescriptor is package-private and never instantiated or referenced anywhere in the snapshot, so the path is dead code, not an exploitable vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: CronMapper's ValueMappingFieldExpressionVisitor drops the inner expression of Every (ValueMappingFieldExpressionVisitor.java:57-59) and On retains nth; CronMapper.weekDayMapping can throw via WeekDay/ConstantsMapper for unusual custom definitions.
rejected_leads.reason: Correctness/semantic issues with no demonstrated security boundary or attacker-controlled input; not strong enough to report.

summary: Reviewed the cron-utils 9.1.5 source snapshot (109 visible files: 87 Java sources under src/main/java, i18n bundles, build/CI files; no test sources are present). The strongest distinct issue traced is in the optional Bean Validation integration: `CronValidator.isValid` feeds an exception message that embeds the raw, user-supplied cron string directly into `ConstraintValidatorContext.buildConstraintViolationWithTemplate(...)`, i.e. untrusted data is used as a validation message *template*, the classic CWE-1336/CWE-917 pattern that is evaluated/interpolated by the Bean Validation message interpolator (Hibernate Validator's default ResourceBundleMessageInterpolator evaluates `${...}` EL when an EL implementation is present). A second-class set of robustness/DoS leads (composite `|` parsing ArrayIndexOutOfBounds, `1#` parsing AIOOBE, DateUtils holiday-range infinite recursion, SecondsDescriptor self-recursion in dead code) was inspected but not submitted; they are weaker on impact or reachability, or are unreachable dead code. No code-audit sink for files/exec/deserialization exists in this tree.
